title: Secondary helix contact topology: reaction reversal and slotted-vs-selected-flank mechanics
scientific_question: When the required secondary helix reaction reverses sign, where does that occur, which physical terms cause it, and only after the mechanism is understood, does bilateral zero-clearance slotted support materially change transient CVT behavior relative to a physically released selected flank?

reference_topology.name: bilateral_zero_clearance_slot
reference_topology.policy: Use the shared results reference model. Preserve the production signed helix torque/force law, torsional spring, movable-member inertia, shaft reaction, and kinematic coupling. Negative selected-flank reaction is carried by the opposite slot flank.

primary_contact_quantity.name: helix_reacted_torque_margin_Nm
primary_contact_quantity.interpretation: positive = selected flank compressive; zero = lift-off boundary; negative = opposite slot flank required by the slotted solution

reaction_map.question: Where is the quasi-static selected-flank zero-reaction boundary in shift-position / secondary-belt-torque space?

forward_control.question: Does ordinary forward operation approach or cross the selected-flank reaction boundary under the slotted reference topology?

stress_screen.question: Which naturally reachable shift states and smooth signed secondary-torque ramps generate clean near-zero or sign-reversing helix reaction trajectories?

hill_entry.question: Can a sudden road-load increase create or deepen opposite-flank demand under the ordinary Baja engine and vehicle boundary?

downhill_engine_braking.question: When the vehicle can drive the CVT and the primary boundary transitions from full throttle to resisting torque, does M_h reverse and which term causes it?

bench_backdrive.question: With the vehicle removed, can a driven secondary shaft cleanly force reverse power flow and a helix reaction reversal?

bench_resisting_load.question: With the vehicle removed, how does a direct resisting secondary load approach the selected-flank boundary from different ratios and a high-dynamic natural state?

dynamic_restart.selection: Natural engaged sample maximizing |shaft-accel term| + |shift-accel term| + |curvature term|.
dynamic_restart.purpose: Give helix inertial terms a deliberate chance to control the zero crossing rather than only belt torque.

scenario_discovery.question: Across road-load, reverse-power-flow, engine-braking, bench-drive, and high-dynamic initial states, which mechanisms produce clean and substantial opposite-flank demand?

cases.description: Exact physical grade programme used by run_dynamic_actuator_ablation.py --scenario hill: 10 s flat, 2 s rise to 30 deg, 10 s at 30 deg, then the tagged default continuation.
Full natural launch followed by a deliberately harder hill from the evolved vehicle/CVT state.

legacy_hill_replays.question: Does a naturally evolved full-launch hill trajectory reproduce the unilateral helix lift-off condition seen in earlier hill studies, and if so where and why?

vehicle_envelope.reference_scale_definition: Magnitude no larger than the pinned engine boundary configured maximum braking torque. This is an engine-scale bound, not a validated closed-throttle torque map at every speed.
vehicle_envelope.question: For naturally reached mid-range ratios and downhill grades, at what primary braking torque does the full dynamic selected-flank margin cross zero, and is that threshold inside the reference engine-scale braking magnitude?

dynamic_ramp_refinement.selection: For each ratio/grade pair, choose a coarse vehicle point with positive quasi-static margin closest to the full boundary, preferring reference-scale braking when available.
dynamic_ramp_refinement.strict_dynamic_only_definition: minimum full M_h < 0 while minimum trajectory-frozen M_h,QS > 0 over the resolved post-onset case.
dynamic_ramp_refinement.question: Can transient helix inertia alone move an otherwise quasi-statically admissible vehicle case through the selected-flank boundary, preferably without belt-slip switching or travel-stop impact?

bench_dynamic_novelty.restart: natural sample maximizing helix dynamic-term magnitude
bench_dynamic_novelty.question: Around the E4 inertia-dominated back-drive discovery, is there a cleaner mechanism-isolation case where the full dynamic helix crosses zero while M_h,QS remains positive?

novelty_metrics.M_h_QS: belt reacted torque + torsional spring torque
novelty_metrics.strict_dynamic_only_case: minimum full M_h < 0 and minimum M_h,QS > 0 over the resolved post-onset case
novelty_metrics.dynamic_only_at_first_full_crossing: M_h,QS > 0 at the linearly interpolated first full M_h crossing

selected_flank_comparator.requirement: Release both helix contact reaction and helix kinematic constraint at lift-off; introduce independent movable-member relative rotation during detachment.
selected_flank_comparator.forbidden_shortcut: Do not use force clipping with theta=theta(s) as the primary physical comparator.

topology_vehicle_cases.question: For representative realistic and bench cases, what trajectory consequence follows from slotted support versus true selected-flank detachment?

discovery_metrics.D_opp_engaged: measure(M_h < 0) / time with a resolved engaged helix margin
discovery_metrics.zero_crossing_count: number of sign changes in M_h after duplicate event times are resolved
discovery_metrics.first_opposite_flank_time_s: linearly interpolated first M_h=0 crossing into M_h<0

interpretation_boundaries: The slotted reference is a results-programme topology, not a claim that every real CVT should use a slot.
A negative selected-flank margin in the slotted model means opposite-flank support, not a solver failure.
The released CINDER selected-flank topology detects inadmissible tensile reaction but does not model detached motion or opposite-flank capture.
Real backlash, free flight, contact impact, friction, and finite capture dynamics are outside the zero-clearance slotted idealization and the first-order detached comparator.
The exploration stages E1-E4 discover candidate mechanisms; E5 maps lift-off thresholds and explicitly separates full-dynamic from trajectory-frozen quasi-static admissibility.

A dynamic-only E5 event supports the mechanism statement that retained movable-member inertia changes selected-flank admissibility on the same trajectory. It is not by itself a literature-priority claim.
E5 cases use tighter tolerances and denser sampling than broad E4 discovery before any candidate is promoted to topology comparison.
